newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience selects cancer drugs for trials.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience selects cancer drugs for trials.

text.p: Biotechnology firm Chiroscience said on Monday that two new compounds against cancer are to start clinical trials in the fourth quarter of this year.
The two MMP inhibitor development compounds, D1927 and D2163, showed "excellent selectivity and efficacy" in pre-clinical models, Chiroscience said.
"Today's announcement of the selection of two development candidates for cancer is another major step forward for the group," said chief executive John Padfield.
Chiroscience, formed in 1993, said development of Levobupivacaine, a cleaned up version of an existing local anaesthetic, was making "excellent" progress.
The group's novel anti-asthma programme has identified new compounds, while testing of an earlier selected anti-asthma drug, D4418, will start in May.
Chiroscience said the integration of Darwin Molecular Corporation, the U.S. gene-based technology firm acquired last year, is progressing well.
